body: London Heathrow Airport (LHR) has sparked a furious response from Virgin Atlantic after ordering joint venture partner Delta Air Lines to relocate from Terminal 3 to Terminal 4 in 2028. Sky News reports that the decision follows a major review of terminal occupancy, with Virgin warning that separating the airlines could increase fares and undermine competition. The two carriers have shared Terminal 3 since 2016, building an integrated transatlantic operation offering convenient connections and premium facilities.

Virgin chief executive Corneel Koster warned: "If implemented in 2028, Heathrow's decision to separate Delta Air Lines from Virgin Atlantic would create friction for customers, weaken competition, and reduce choice. As all other airports seek to co-locate joint venture partners, Heathrow has chosen to split ours after more than a decade together." The move would complicate connections, potentially increasing transfer times and requiring additional security screening, and premium passengers would lose convenient access to Virgin's Terminal 3 Clubhouse, Upper Class Wing, and Revivals Lounge. Meanwhile, British Airways and American Airlines benefit from substantial co-location at Terminal 5.

Heathrow maintains that its proposals will improve capacity, reduce congestion, and accommodate growth. A Heathrow spokesperson told Sky News: "As demand at Heathrow continues to grow, these small number of moves will unlock more capacity across terminals, reduce congestion, improve the flow of passengers, and help keep costs down." The airport says airlines representing 81% of passengers support the plan, though the British Airways-American Airlines joint venture represents nearly 70% of all Heathrow-US traffic. Virgin says it will consider "all available options" to challenge the outcome, potentially involving the Civil Aviation Authority, the Competition and Markets Authority, or the courts, while Delta has yet to comment publicly.
en.summary: London Heathrow has ordered Delta Air Lines to move from Terminal 3 to Terminal 4 in 2028, splitting its joint venture with Virgin Atlantic after a decade of co-location and drawing a furious response from Virgin.
en.title: Heathrow orders Delta to leave shared Virgin Atlantic terminal in 2028

body: 倫敦希斯洛機場（LHR）下令合資夥伴達美航空於2028年由第三航廈遷往第四航廈，引發維珍航空強烈反彈。根據天空新聞報導，這項決定來自航廈使用的大規模檢討，維珍航空警告，拆散兩家航空公司可能推高票價、削弱競爭。兩家航空公司自2016年起共用第三航廈，建立了整合的跨大西洋營運，提供便利的轉機與高階設施。
維珍航空執行長科斯特警告，若於2028年實施，希斯洛機場拆散達美航空與維珍航空的決定將為旅客製造不便、削弱競爭並減少選擇；他指出，其他機場都設法讓合資夥伴共用航廈，希斯洛卻在合作逾十年後選擇拆散雙方。搬遷將使轉機變複雜，可能拉長轉機時間並需要額外安檢，高階旅客也將失去便利使用維珍航空第三航廈會所、高階艙專屬通道與抵達貴賓室的權益。相較之下，英國航空與美國航空在第五航廈享有大規模共用設施。
希斯洛機場則主張，這項調整將提升容量、紓解壅塞並因應成長。機場發言人向天空新聞表示，隨著希斯洛需求持續成長，少數航廈搬遷將釋出各航廈容量、減少壅塞、改善旅客動線並協助控制成本。機場稱代表81%旅客的航空公司支持這項計畫，但英國航空與美國航空的合資事業占希斯洛往返美國旅客近70%。維珍航空表示將考慮所有可行選項挑戰此結果，可能訴諸民航局、競爭及市場管理局或法院；達美航空目前尚未公開評論。
zh.summary: 倫敦希斯洛機場要求達美航空於2028年由第三航廈遷往第四航廈，拆散與維珍航空長達十年的共用航廈合作，維珍航空強烈反彈，警告此舉將削弱競爭、推高票價。
zh.title: 希斯洛機場（LHR）下令達美航空2028年搬離維珍共用航廈
